review_mode: Independent agent reading of all four exercise pages, exhaustive classical checks and primary-source comparison
result: Scientific conditions, QUBO formulation, optimality argument and probability calculations pass

calculation.execution_level: Classical enumeration and arithmetic; no CP-SAT execution, annealer simulation or QPU execution
checks: Constructed schedule reaches the five-hour job-chain and resource-load lower bounds.
At deadline five hours, all 16384 assignments of 14 logical variables were evaluated; the nonnegative constraint penalties equal the independently expanded quadratic polynomial on every assignment.
Exactly one zero-energy assignment exists, matching the independently checked feasible schedule among all 144 start-time combinations.
At deadline four hours, all 1024 assignments and all 36 start-time combinations were checked; no feasible schedule exists and the minimum penalty energy is two.
For p=0.10 and p=0.02, exact rational powers verify that 29 and 149 trials are the smallest counts reaching 95 percent success under independent stationary sampling.
Fixed cost plus sampling gives 9.45 and 15.45 seconds; 40 samples at p=0.02 succeed with probability 0.554299596049049.
A perfectly correlated Bernoulli-batch counterexample demonstrates why the marginal p alone does not justify the independent-trial formula.

scientific_findings.finding: The nonpreemptive operations occupy half-open intervals [0,2) and [2,5) on alternating resources. Positive feasibility penalties have H=0 exactly for valid schedules. Fourteen is the unpruned logical binary-variable count, not a physical-qubit estimate.

The success criterion combines constraint feasibility with completion by the selected schedule deadline. The sample formula assumes independence and constant p. Maintenance makespan is measured in hours; solver latency is measured in seconds.

The first hypothetical quantum scenario meets the ten-second computation target but is slower than the same-instance two-second classical baseline. Failing to sample a deadline-compliant schedule does not prove infeasibility. A separate lower-bound or exact-solver certificate is needed.

Estimate success uncertainty, inspect dependence and repeat complete batches across instances, embeddings and dates. The proposed confidence-bound and matched-baseline adoption targets are educational choices, not a demonstrated deployment result.
